"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The `manager_restarted` check only compares manager PIDs and invocation IDs. A guest reboot between the `before` and `after` manager snapshots naturally changes both values, so the check can pass without proving a manager restart on the same boot. The separate `boot_id_changed` check covers only the reboot snapshot pair and does not prevent this false positive. Requiring nonempty equal boot IDs in the manager snapshot pair, while retaining the PID and invocation-ID checks, is a routine correctness fix.
